items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: So Lincoln Center -- they called. The Lincoln Center Library -- they finally called. And there was some star photographer, John Stones, he wanted to -- he was employed by, I think, the Lincoln Center Library to make a story, to take a film of these tap dancers.

ctx.x: So, the next thing I knew, I was called to come out to the box office. And I had to converse with -- which we call Dada. And he said, how would you like to go on the television, you see. And I went on the television with Joe Franklin, you see. So, it happened that once, and then I got invited to return. So, I had to go back again.

So, now all of this is happening to get to these tap dancers, you see. So Lincoln Center -- they called. The Lincoln Center Library -- they finally called. And there was some star photographer, John Stones, he wanted to -- he was employed by, I think, the Lincoln Center Library to make a

story, to take a film of these tap dancers.
Now, this is during the time of the Olympics. One of the members -- in fact -- yeah -- one of the members and a future member was committed to perform on this tour with the Olympics, you see. They had to go to Japan, Africa, I think, Mexico and so forth -- Spain -- somewhere in there, you know. And then they come back to America.
